on_shelf.label: Philosophy of Right §33
on_shelf.text: The thought idea of the good is realized both in the will turned back into itself, and also in the external world. Thus freedom exists as real substance, which is quite as much actuality and necessity as it is subjective will. The idea here is its absolutely universal existence, viz., ethical observance. This ethical substance is again, a. Natural spirit; the family, 6.

on_shelf.label: Philosophie des Rechts §33
on_shelf.text: C. die Einheit und Wahrheit dieser bsiden abstrakten Momente, — die gedachte Idee des Guten realisiert in dem in sich reflektierten Willen und in äußerlicher Welt; ■ — so daß die Freiheit als die Substanz ebensosehr als Wirklichkeit und Notwendigkeit existiert, wie als subjektiver Wille; — die Idee in ihrer an und für sich allgemeinen Existenz; die Sittlichkeit.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Good morning, Ramesh. The tea is welcome. I trust the household is quiet this morning; I shall take my reading to the step before the sun grows too strong.

typed_records.speaker: Ramesh
typed_records.words: Morning, Shri Hegel. Yes, quiet as a library. I’ll have the breakfast ready by seven, if you don’t mind.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: I shall begin the walk now, Ramesh. Thank you for the tea. I will return before the heat settles.

typed_records.speaker: Ramesh
typed_records.words: All right, sir. The gate is unlocked, so you just walk out. I'll keep the sambar warm.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: Mr. Malhotra, you have served the state for three decades. In my lectures, I argue that the state is the actuality of the ethical idea. But you, who have lived within its apparatus, what did it feel like to witness the Idea move through the machinery of bureaucracy? Was there a moment when the machinery seemed to move of its own accord, independent of the spirit it was meant to serve?

typed_records.speaker: Mr. R. K. Malhotra
typed_records.words: I don't know what a 'spirit' is, but I know the difference between a file and a decision. The machinery doesn't move, it waits. You have to push it, and even then, it usually just creaks.

typed_records.speaker: Hegel
typed_records.words: You mistake the nature of the thing, sir. A machine is dead; it requires a hand from outside to move it. The state is not a machine, but a living organism, the actuality of the ethical idea. It does not creak because it is pushed; it moves because the spirit within it recognizes its own freedom. Your file is stuck not because the machinery is broken, but because it has not yet found the form that corresponds to its content. It must be allowed to grow into its decision, not forced.
